findings.failure_path: If the victim fails only while running concurrently with A, or intermittently regardless of predecessors, there is no stable set of tests that “run before it.” Single subset runs can nevertheless mark an arbitrary half as failing, discard A, and report a minimal but spurious polluting subsequence. The later generic flakiness guidance does not guard this mandatory reduction step, and the cited delta-debugging excerpt does not justify the serial-suite assumption.
findings.smallest_fix: Restrict this recipe to a repeatedly reproducible failure under a fixed serial order. For flaky or parallel execution, require preserving the failing schedule and validating each retained/rejected subset over repeated runs with a stated threshold; otherwise route to concurrency or statistical diagnosis. Narrow the source attribution to input reduction unless a primary source supporting suite-polluter reduction is supplied.

concern_results.conclusion: The suite-reduction rule assumes a stable serial failure predicate. Parallel or flaky suite failures can therefore select a false polluter or eliminate the real concurrent peer. The supplied source excerpt supports delta reduction of inputs, but not this unconditional extension to ordered test suites.

challenge_focus: Adversarial focus (continuation chain r5): the order-preserving delta-debugging recipe — can an agent following it literally stall, discard a required polluter, or falsely clear a suite; consistency of every duplicated rule between SKILL.md and the playbook (probe ordering, boundary walk, bisect narrowing, upstream trace, suite reduction); gate-fireability and bypass-by-omission of the new rules; data-leak or data-loss paths in instrumentation and persisted evidence; contradictions with falsify-first, three-strike, complexity-verdict, and sanitization rules; over-broad absolutes on simple bugs; accuracy of Sources and attribution-evidence excerpts against the primary pages.
